operations.name: Calcinatio
operations.description: The reduction of a substance to ash or powder by sustained heat. Corresponds to Fire. Destroys the fixed, releases the volatile.
operations.latin_desc: Calcinatio est operatio qua corpus in calcem vel cinerem redigitur per ignis actionem continuatam. Per hanc operationem fixum destruitur et volatile liberatur.

operations.name: Solutio
operations.description: The dissolving of a solid substance in a liquid solvent. Corresponds to Water. What was fixed becomes fluid, what was hidden is revealed.
operations.latin_desc: Solutio est operatio qua solidum in liquorem resolvitur. Quod erat fixum, fluidum fit; quod occultum erat, revelatur.

operations.name: Separatio
operations.description: The separation of the pure from the impure, the subtle from the gross. Corresponds to Air. The three principles (Sulfur, Mercury, Salt) are distinguished.
operations.latin_desc: Separatio est operatio qua purum ab impuro, subtile a spisso separatur. Tria principia — Sulphur, Mercurius, Sal — distinguuntur.

operations.name: Coniunctio
operations.description: The union of opposites: male and female, Sol and Luna, Sulfur and Mercury. The hierosgamos of alchemy, producing the hermaphroditic Stone.
operations.latin_desc: Coniunctio est unio oppositorum: masculi et feminae, Solis et Lunae, Sulphuris et Mercurii. Est hierosgamos alchymiae, ex quo lapis hermaphroditus producitur.

operations.name: Fermentatio
operations.description: The introduction of a spiritualizing agent (the ferment) that transforms the entire substance. Like yeast in bread, the ferment works invisibly.
operations.latin_desc: Fermentatio est operatio qua fermentum spiritualizans in corpus introducitur quod totam substantiam transformet. Ut fermentum in pane, sic lapis fermentat.

operations.name: Distillatio
operations.description: The purification by repeated vaporization and condensation. The spirit rises and falls, becoming ever purer. Corresponds to the philosophical Mercury.
operations.latin_desc: Distillatio est purificatio per vaporationem et condensationem iteratas. Spiritus ascendit et descendit, semper purior factus. Respondet Mercurio philosophico.

operations.name: Coagulatio
operations.description: The fixation of the volatile, the embodiment of the spirit. What was fluid becomes solid, permanently. The final sealing of the Stone's power.
operations.latin_desc: Coagulatio est fixatio volatilis, incorporatio spiritus. Quod fluidum erat, solidum fit permanenter. Est sigillatio ultima potentiae lapidis.

substances.name: Sulphur Philosophorum
substances.description: The active, fiery, solar principle. Not common sulfur, but the sulfurous spirit hidden in all metals — the principle of fixity and color.
substances.latin_desc: Sulphur philosophicum est principium activum, igneum, solare. Non est sulphur commune, sed spiritus sulphureus in omnibus metallis latens.

substances.name: Mercurius Philosophorum
substances.description: The passive, volatile, lunar principle. The dissolving water, the universal solvent, the spirit that mediates between body and soul.
substances.latin_desc: Mercurius philosophicus est principium passivum, volatile, lunare. Aqua dissolvens, menstruum universale, spiritus inter corpus et animam medians.

substances.name: Sal Philosophorum
substances.description: The body, the earth, the principle of fixity and resistance. The matrix in which Sulfur and Mercury combine. Paracelsus added this as the third principle.
substances.latin_desc: Sal philosophicum est corpus, terra, principium fixitatis et resistentiae. Matrix in qua Sulphur et Mercurius coniguntur. Paracelsus hoc tertium principium addidit.

substances.name: Plumbum
substances.description: The base metal of Saturn, cold and heavy. The prima materia of alchemical work, associated with the prima materia of Creation itself.
substances.latin_desc: Plumbum est metallum Saturni, frigidum et grave. Prima materia operis alchymici, primae materiae Creationis associatum.

substances.name: Ferrum
substances.description: The metal of Mars, hard and martial. Rules blood, weapons, and the vital heat of organisms. More resistant to transmutation than lead.
substances.latin_desc: Ferrum est metallum Martis, durum et martiale. Sanguini, armis et calori vitali praesidet.

substances.name: Cuprum
substances.description: The metal of Venus, the most beautiful of the base metals. Rules love, harmony, and the generative power of nature.
substances.latin_desc: Cuprum est metallum Veneris, pulcherrimum ex metallis imperfectis. Amori, harmoniae et vi generativae naturae praesidet.

substances.name: Argentum
substances.description: The metal of the Moon, almost perfect. Pure silver is one step from gold and bears the nature of the lunar Mercury.
substances.latin_desc: Argentum est metallum Lunae, propemodum perfectum. Argentum purum uno gradu distat ab auro et naturam Mercurii lunaris gerit.

substances.name: Aurum
substances.description: The perfect metal of the Sun. The philosopher's goal is not gold but the process that produces it — the Stone which can transmute all base metals into gold.
substances.latin_desc: Aurum est metallum perfectum Solis. Finis philosophi non est aurum sed processus qui id producit — lapis qui omnia metalla imperfecta in aurum transmutare valet.

substances.name: Vitriolum
substances.description: Green vitriol (iron sulfate) or blue vitriol (copper sulfate). The acid that dissolves metals, an agent of Solutio. Its alchemical acronym: Visita Interiora Terrae Rectificando Invenies Occultum Lapidem.
substances.latin_desc: Vitriolum viride vel caeruleum. Acidum quod metalla dissolvit. Acronymum alchymicum: Visita Interiora Terrae Rectificando Invenies Occultum Lapidem.

substances.name: Nitrum
substances.description: Potassium nitrate, the fire-salt. Used in Calcinatio and Fermentatio. Associated with the fiery explosive power in the earth.
substances.latin_desc: Nitrum est sal ignis. In calcinatione et fermentatione adhibetur. Vi explosivae igneae in terra associatur.

combinations.description: Lead calcined to its ash — a grey-white powder. The first step in working with Saturn's metal. The fixed nature of lead is broken, releasing its spirit.
combinations.latin_result: Plumbum calcinatum in pulverem cinereum album conversum est. Prima gradus in opere Saturnino.

combinations.description: Lead dissolved in acid — becomes minium (red lead) when further worked. The Solutio of lead is an important step in the white work.
combinations.latin_result: Plumbum in acidum solutum est et in minium conversuri sumus.

combinations.description: Calcined iron yields a red-orange ochre — the blood-color of Mars. This tincture communicates martial virtues and was used in medical operations.
combinations.latin_result: Ferrum calcinatum ochram rubro-aranteam producit — colorem sanguinis Martis.

combinations.description: The conjunction of Philosophical Sulfur and Mercury is the royal marriage — the first formation of the Stone in its immature state. It must still be fermented and fixed.
combinations.latin_result: Sulphur et Mercurius philosophici coniuncti sunt in matrimonium regium. Lapis inchoatus formatus est.

combinations.description: Mercury rectified by repeated distillation becomes the universal dissolvent — the menstruum that can dissolve even gold. Seven distillations are required.
combinations.latin_result: Mercurius per distillationes iteratas rectificatus menstruum universale factus est. Septem distillationes requiruntur.

combinations.description: Vitriol dissolved in water yields the famous green vitriol solution — a strong acid used to dissolve other metals. The green lion of the alchemists.
combinations.latin_result: Vitriolum in aquam solutum aquam viridem producit — leonem viridem alchymistarum.

combinations.description: Silver conjoined with Philosophical Sulfur becomes the fixed White Stone — the lesser accomplishment of the opus, able to transmute base metals to silver.
combinations.latin_result: Argentum cum Sulphure philosophico coniunctum Lapidem Album Fixum producit — opus minus completum.

combinations.description: Niter used as a ferment introduces the fiery aerial spirit into the work — the 'food of fire' that accelerates all transformations.
combinations.latin_result: Nitrum ut fermentum spiritum igneum aërium in opus introducit — 'cibum ignis' quod omnes transformationes accelerat.
